queries.query: AI Medical Jazz contouring radiotherapy France vendor product
Federau neuroradiological reading multiple sclerosis follow-up MRI intelligent automation

findings.observation: Jazz is described on the vendor's own site as a neuroradiology 'lesion tracking and reporting' tool for diagnostic MS follow-up (single-click annotation, volumetric lesion tracking, automated report generation) — it is not a radiotherapy organ/target auto-contouring product. Its sole supporting publication (Federau et al., Neuroradiology 2024) evaluates diagnostic MS-lesion reading productivity/quality, not RT contouring. Classifying Jazz under 'Auto-Contouring' (an RT category) alongside true OAR/target contouring tools like Limbus or MVision is a category-fit mismatch.
findings.suggestedFix: Re-examine whether Jazz belongs in the Auto-Contouring (radiotherapy) category at all, or whether it should be reclassified/footnoted as a diagnostic neuroradiology tool with only tangential RT relevance. At minimum, the impact rationale should state explicitly that the supporting evidence is diagnostic, not RT-contouring, evidence.

findings.observation: L3 clinical impact label for Jazz is derived from a diagnostic-radiology productivity study, not a radiotherapy planning/dosimetric study — applying an RT clinical-impact tier to non-RT evidence risks a false 'clean' L3 impact rating.
findings.suggestedFix: Down-grade or re-derive the impact label using RT-specific criteria, or mark impact as not-applicable/out-of-scope for RT auto-contouring comparisons.

findings.observation: static-audit.json title/rationale for this DOI reads 'Multi-vendor auto-contouring comparison across 5 facilities' and 'Multi-centre evaluation across five facilities including review and edit effort,' with multiCenter:true in both score and qualityFlags. The actual paper (Goddard et al. 2024) is a SINGLE-institution study: all nine authors are affiliated with Montefiore Medical Center / Albert Einstein College of Medicine, using one Siemens-SOMATOMgo scanner and 47 patients — there is no mention of '5 facilities' anywhere in the title, abstract, or author affiliations. This fabricated 'five facilities' / 'multi-centre' claim inflates both the evidentiary rigor (contributing to the E2 rating) and the multiCenter/externalValidation quality flags for mim-contour-protegeai.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct title field to 'Evaluation of multiple-vendor AI autocontouring solutions', remove the fabricated '5 facilities'/multi-centre framing from the rationale, set multiCenter:false in both score.rigorSource and qualityFlags, and re-assess whether E2 rigor is still warranted for a single-institution, single-scanner, 47-patient study (likely should drop toward E1 unless other corroborating multi-site evidence is added).

findings.observation: Top-level qualityFlags.multiCenter:true for mim-contour-protegeai is a false 'clean' flag directly caused by the fabricated '5 facilities' claim above; this flag should not be marked true/passing.
findings.suggestedFix: Set qualityFlags.multiCenter to false and re-derive computedRigor accordingly.
